Intermediate-acting (Humulin N Kwikpen/Vial, Novolin N Flexpen/Vial) and short-acting (Humulin R Vial/Kwikpen, Novolin R Flexpen/Vial) subsections list items only in the left/preferred column with no corresponding non-preferred entries -- read as all-preferred for those two subsections. Mixed insulins: Humalog Mix 50-50 Kwikpen, Humalog Mix 75-25 Vial, Humulin 70-30 Vial, Insulin Lispro Protamine Mix 75-25 Pen, NovoLog Mix 70-30 Flexpen/Vial PREFERRED; Humalog Mix 75-25 Kwikpen, Humulin 70-30 Kwikpen, Novolin 70-30 (all forms) NON-PREFERRED -- note the same premixed product (Humalog Mix 75-25, Humulin 70-30) is preferred in Vial form but non-preferred in Kwikpen-pen form, a device-specific split. records.verificationNote: Read live from the Highmark Comprehensive Formulary search tool (siteCode=8103967260; Formulary Effective Date 07/24/2026). Searched 'insulin glargine' and 'insulin lispro'; opened both 'Endocrine | Insulin Analogs - Long Acting' (24 rows) and 'Endocrine | Insulin Analogs - Rapid Acting' (27 rows) class listings and read every row. No insulin product anywhere in either class is Tier 1 — Tier 2 is the best available tier for this whole category. The plain-labeled generic 'Insulin Glargine' pen/solution is Tier 2 with no PA (same tier as brand Lantus), so it was picked as the single preferredAgent. A real brand-over-generic tier gap was found and documented: generic insulin lispro, insulin aspart, insulin degludec, and insulin glargine-yfgn are all Tier 3/non-formulary (insulin degludec additionally PA-flagged) while their brand counterparts (Humalog, NovoLog, Tresiba) sit at Tier 2 with no PA — the opposite of the usual generic-preferred pattern, most likely driven by manufacturer rebate contracts rather than a clinical BOGL exception. Confirmed vs inferred: all tiers/PA icons directly read from the live tool for both classes.
